newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CROWN NERVOUS AS MARKET DIGESTS TRADE DATA.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CROWN NERVOUS AS MARKET DIGESTS TRADE DATA.

text.p: The Czech crown was little changed but dealers were quoting wide-spreads on Monday morning after the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) said April's trade deficit grew to 15.3 billion crowns from 13.1 billion in March.
Just after the announcemnt, the crown was trading at around minus 3.0 percent below the mid-point of its mark/dollar basket from minus 2.6 percent before the trade figures were released.

"It's kind of a confirmation of the trend that the deficit is growing at the same pace...that the only way is that the economy must work better and it will not do that under these interest rates and the only thing is to devalue," said Petr Kukla of Girocredit Bank.
Kukla said spreads of between 50 and 100 basis points were being quoted as dealing rooms anlaysed the data and decided what course of action to take.
The crown was under heavy pressure last week from speculative sellers forcing the central bank to intervene heavily to prop up the currency.
The central bank has also raised the repo rate to around 75 percent from 12.9 percent and closed off access to the last resort Lombard rate.

At the same time, the centre-right governing coalition is undergoing a shake up with three senior ministers, including Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, announcing over the weekend that they would step down.
